I am 58 years old, farming in Quzhou County for 30 years. I finished middle school and came straight back to the land. My household has six people — my son and daughter-in-law work in the factory in town, so when it gets busy I hire two workers from the village to help. I have 12.4 mu and a well, so I can irrigate when the sky refuses to rain.

I never start from a blank sheet. I look at what I did last year and fix what went wrong. Last year my cotton was hit hard by bollworm in August, and I only got 240 jin per mu. My neighbor Lao Zhang planted a hybrid variety and sprayed five times — he got over 300 jin per mu. So this year I will plant hybrid cotton on 5 mu, and I will spray five times, not four. For fertilizer, I will put one bag of compound fertilizer — 50 kilograms — as base dressing when I plough in April. Then I will topdress with 25 kilograms of urea and 15 kilograms of potassium chloride per mu during flowering and boll stage. That is about 20 jin of nitrogen per mu. I know it is a lot of money — a bag of urea is over 100 yuan now — but I would rather waste some fertilizer than watch my cotton turn yellow and lose yield. A bad harvest means I cannot pay for my grandson's school fees.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October on 3.5 mu. At green-up I already spread 15 kilograms of urea per mu. I will irrigate three times — once now at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain fill — and spray twice for aphids and rust. If the weather holds, I expect 450 kilograms per mu. As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I plant hybrid maize the same day — no time to waste. I put 40 kilograms of compound fertilizer in the drill at planting, then 20 kilograms of urea at the big trumpet stage. Two irrigations for maize should be enough if the summer rains come, and I will spray three times for armyworm and corn borer. I expect 550 kilograms per mu.

Peanut goes on 2.4 mu. I switched to an improved variety three years ago because the pods are bigger than the traditional kind. I rotary-till and put 30 kilograms of compound fertilizer plus 20 kilograms of superphosphate per mu — peanuts need that calcium. Two irrigations, three pesticide sprays, and I should get 300 kilograms per mu.

Mung bean is on the last 1.5 mu. I save my own seed, the same traditional variety my father used. Mung bean does not need much — 10 kilograms of compound fertilizer per mu, one irrigation if July is dry, and two sprays for pod borer. I expect 100 kilograms per mu. If the price is good I sell it; if not, I feed it to the chickens.

I learned these amounts by watching what works in my own field and copying the neighbors who do well. The input dealer tells me the numbers on the bag, but I adjust based on what I see. If everyone around me is using similar fertilizer and getting green, thick crops, I do the same. Changing too much is dangerous — last year I tried saving money on peanut fertilizer and the pods were small. Never again.
